**It is also the retcon that explains the cabin.** Every vanilla
object in this ship -- the fridge, the oven, the counters, the
theatre chair, the lamp, the lockers, the television -- has never had
an in-fiction reason to be aboard a Starfleet shuttle. Now it does:
she collected them. The survey specialist furnished her field station
with what she was studying, and her department calls that method. One
tape, and twenty-four squares of borrowed PZ furniture stop being a
compromise and become a character trait.
It ends by planting Section 31 **without naming it**, because the
misdirection has to be honestly reasoned rather than a lie: a hidden
outpost with no relay and no traffic really is the shape of something
deniable, and she is right about that and wrong about who did it.

title: Personal Log: Entry One
subtitle: Lt. Lucy Shepard, cultural survey, U.S.S. Adirondack
author: recorded aboard this shuttle
extra: Ten February. For whoever is standing in my cabin.

lines.text: PERSONAL LOG: LT. LUCY SHEPARD
CULTURAL SURVEY DETACHMENT, U.S.S. ADIRONDACK
DAY TWO. TEN FEBRUARY, LOCAL RECKONING
If you are watching this, you are in my shuttle.
Everything in here is mine. I will explain the fridge.
Start at the beginning. I asked for this posting.
Nobody asks for this posting. I asked for it twice.
THE WORLD
A world so like Earth the first survey was recalled.
They logged it as a sensor fault. It was not.
Same continents, near enough, and about the same century.
Combustion engines. Magnetic tape. No global network.
They have a Kentucky. A Kentucky.
My job was to watch and write it down.
THE CABIN
Which brings me to the fridge, and everything else.
You cannot understand a people from orbit. So I furnished.
All of it came up from down there, logged item by item.
The counters. The lockers. The lamp. The television.
I ate what they ate. I sat the way they sit.
My department calls that method. The ship called it clutter.
The television is the best thing I ever carried up.
It plays tape. So I put everything I love onto tape.
Favourite videos. Holos, flattened. Transcripts, read out.
All of it dubbed down onto magnetic tape, like a local.
There is a rack of them by the screen. Any order you like.
THE WORK
Beam down at dawn, beam up before dark. Six months of it.
Market days. Radio broadcasts. A couple weddings.
I was going to get a paper out of this. A good one.
She stops. Something is beeping off camera. She ignores it.
AND THEN THE NINTH
On the ninth of February we lost the Adirondack.
She is damaged. She is still up there.
So there is some hope, I suppose.
A hundred and forty-one of us. She cannot leave.
Nothing attacked her. Nothing was on sensors at all.
Eleven of us were on the surface. We still are.
So far down there, nothing is wrong.
The markets opened this morning. The radio is playing.
I am stranded above a world having an ordinary week.
ON THE RECORD
Starfleet does not know we are here. That was deliberate.
A hidden outpost. No relay, no traffic, nothing filed.
I used to think that was good tradecraft.
I have had a lot of time to think about who benefits.
I am going to keep recording. Somebody should.
END OF ENTRY ONE
